pages.observation: Layout: one wide panel across the top, then a tall panel at lower left and a tall panel at lower right. My natural order: P1 caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' (top left), then the teal label 'NOW · A-12' (top right). Then P2 caption 'A quick vitals check first.', then the balloon 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' Its tail drops straight down to the nurse placeholder, so the speaker is the nurse. Then P3 caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.', then the teal label 'RAVI · READY' near the bottom of P3. Left to right gives a clear order and no balloons compete for position. Speaker: only one balloon, the nurse's, and the tail goes to the right placeholder. It ends just above the box, not into Ravi. Issues: (1) No screen is drawn in the storyboard, so I cannot check here that 'NOW · A-12' and 'RAVI · READY' sit on screens. The meera placeholder is just below the A-12 label and fairly close to it. (2) The jumps from waiting room to vitals station to the doctor rest entirely on the captions. P3's caption reads like a cut to another room or a parallel moment, which is acceptable. (3) P2 and P3 have a lot of empty space in their lower halves, and 'RAVI · READY' breaks after the dot. Neither causes a reading problem. I found nothing in the order or the speaker that needs a change.

pages.observation: Order: P1 caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' (top left, over the window and waiting chairs). Then my eye moves right across Ravi, who stands in a green shirt with a shoulder bag looking up and right, to 'NOW · A-12' on the wall monitor at top right. The receptionist (Meera) sits below it at a desk. Then P2 caption 'A quick vitals check first.', then the balloon 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' The tail points down to the top of the nurse's head; she is in lilac scrubs, smiling and holding the pump bulb. Then P3 caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.', with the doctor (white coat, stethoscope) looking down at a tablet, then 'RAVI · READY' on the tablet. Speakers: the only balloon belongs to the nurse and its tail is correct. It does not cover her face, the hair just touches the tail point. Ravi's face, the cuff, the pulse oximeter and the monitor are all clear. Ravi looking up toward the monitor connects A-12 to him, and his bag moves to the floor beside his chair in P2. Issues: (1) 'RAVI · READY': the box is on the tablet screen, but its lower edge hangs a little past the tablet's bottom frame onto the bezel. It also covers a drawn status card with a check mark underneath, so two cards stack, one of them half hidden. The break after the dot ('RAVI ·' / 'READY') reads a little awkwardly. Fitting the label inside the screen, or covering the drawn card cleanly, is recommended. (2) 'NOW · A-12' sits on the monitor and covers its whole content area. Its left edge comes very close to the monitor frame, which is acceptable. (3) A reader could take the A-12 slot as Ravi's only by inference from his look upward; nothing on the panel says so. Minor. (4) Place changes (waiting room, vitals station, doctor's room) are carried by the captions and the backgrounds and read clearly. No captions or balloons cover any faces or hands. Result: reading order and the speaker are clear. Item 1 is the only overlap worth fixing.
